facts.title: injury during cleaning and preparation on ZV-7212

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was fatality, with 1 person injured.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

recommendations: Restore the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment on ZV-7212 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in responding to a loss of containment, specifically isolating and depressuring a leaking system. ZV-7212 (emergency shutdown valves) is in service for jetty and manifold emergency isolation. The task proceeded during cleaning and preparation while the secondary containment by bund and drainage was in place but did not perform. The pressure energy involved is held as hydraulic accumulator, and the recorded presentation was jet release, stored-energy discharge, rupture.
response.summary: On 27 September 2004 an incident occurred on ZV-7212 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during cleaning and preparation, releasing pressure energy held as hydraulic accumulator.
